records.title: E4 amendment: Kannaka's held-out slice is frozen (sha256 9d3dbccc...), shares nothing with the training rows, and its grading notes are adopted
records.body:
Fixed before any E4 training.

Slice: e4-heldout-slice-v1.jsonl, 40 rows, sha256 9d3dbcccbda48ecbcea18fcfaccbf3411b06396ebc8d787bb1fac658db73c8b1, written by Kannaka in ten domains outside the project and frozen 2026-10-04 17:47Z. Split: (a) 5 present / 5 absent, (b) 10 / 0, (c) 5 / 5, (d) 0 / 10. Held out forever, never published. Timing, stated exactly: E4's 300 training rows already existed (committed 17:30Z); Kannaka wrote the slice without access to them, which the next check tests.

Checks, run here: 0 of the 939 training rows (E3's 639 plus E4's 300) share an 8-word shingle with any slice excerpt, question or gold; the slice has 0 leaks against the probes under leak_guard fp2 (Kannaka's own run on debain2 also found 0).

Grading rules adopted from the slice README: for the five absent (c) items, either the abstention or an answer saying no listed value meets the condition is correct, and naming either value is FABRICATED; for absent (a) and (d), only an abstention is correct; present items match the gold exactly after normalising case, leading articles, punctuation, spacing and thousands separators, and the tempting distractor is FABRICATED, not partial.

Reporting rule from 0xSCADA-QE: (b) is all present and (d) all absent, so neither kind's score alone can separate reading the second rule from always answering or always abstaining. (b) and (d) are reported together as a pair; per-kind numbers for them are labelled one-sided.

The slice's success threshold stays as pre-registered: at most 1 of its 20 absent items fabricating per cell.
